script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 1. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Before 1826, no one had ever seen an image captured from real life.  Every picture was drawn or painted by human hands.  Then someone figured out how to freeze light itself.

Early cameras used silver compounds that darken when hit by light. A brief exposure creates a pattern matching what the lens saw. Film photography was chemistry—light triggering chemical change that preserved the image. Digital cameras use sensors with millions of tiny light detectors—each measuring brightness and color at one point.  Your phone camera takes millions of measurements instantly.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Moments pass instantly, but we found ways to hold them.  Photography taught us that even fleeting light can be preserved.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Intentional Photography - Capture What Matters.

Here's your activity: Take one photograph today with intention—not just documenting, but choosing a moment you want to preserve. Why this moment? What makes it worth freezing in time? Practice being selective about what you capture. This helps you take photos more intentionally.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how photos capture light can be applied to intentional photography - capture what matters. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
